messages.subject: Trouble finding a suitable model
messages.body_plain:
Hello all!

I am currently analysing movement data of bats and this is the best selected model via ctmm.select() for a singular night.
As you can all see, there is a peak in my data, followed by a plunge, when the bat is returning to its roost. This peak is not acknowledged in the model whatsoever, creating a high percentage of my data, which is not explained by the model.

I, for sure, also know, that this is not an artifact, as the bat shows a similar pattern for the other nights it was observed.

Any ideas on how I can fit a better model?
Or is CTMM not capable of fitting a suitable one to my data?

Thank you in advance!

Janine

messages.subject: Re: Calibration Data for Error Model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Christen,
I conducted a small calibration data collection for my gps collars. I stationed 3 collars in an open field location and 3 collars in an hedgerow adjacent location. Each collar collected 72 fixes in total over two days.
I looked at model selection values for individual collars in both habitats and thankfully, the individual error models had very similar results to joint models.
I then compared joint habitat model selection values with individual habitat model selection values and this was the result I got:

Vertical values are very similar, however there is a moderate difference between the horizontal AICc values. The difference in reduced z-squared value is relatively small. In your vignette for error data, you caution against selecting based on AICc values, if differences are somewhat similar. Do you think these differences necessitate a larger collection of gps in both habitats ?

Thanks for your help,
Aaron

messages.subject: Re: Trouble finding a suitable model
messages.body_plain:
Hi Janine,

That fit actually looks very good. The latter half of the variogram is very noisy, which is why it isn't plotted by default. You can improve the CIs on the empirical variogram with CI="Gauss" if the data are not too irregularly sampled. I assume the point estimates for the theoretical and empirical variograms will still be inside each other's CIs where the empirical variogram is reliable. That's what I would consider to be a very good fit. Substantial white space where the CIs don't overlap is what I would consider to be a bad fit.

Best,
Chris
